sections.overview: Micromalthus debilis is a tiny wood-boring beetle and the sole living species of Micromalthidae.
sections.identification: Winged adults are rarely encountered; some reproductive females retain a larva-like form, so the beetle is often found as larvae or larviform females.
sections.habitat: Its larvae develop in damp, decaying wood, especially fallen or damaged timber; the species is native to eastern North America and has been transported elsewhere with wood.
sections.diet: Larvae bore through decaying wood associated with fungi; the sources describe this substrate rather than a narrow prey-based diet.
sections.behavior: A colony can remain larval for much of the year, with larval females producing live young without mating, a rare form of paedogenesis.
sections.reproduction: Most reproduction is viviparous and parthenogenetic in larviform females; winged adults and males occur in a complex, comparatively uncommon phase.
sections.ecology: By living in decaying wood, it participates in wood decomposition; it may also infest persistently damp structural timber, which explains its common name.
sections.conservation: The sources consulted provide no global conservation assessment or population trend for this beetle.
